note: How two texts differ, defined to the letter (TextDiff.cs): code points; the longest common prefix, then the longest common suffix of what is left; the middle by longest common subsequence, an equal choice inserting before deleting; a hunk is a maximal run of unmatched characters. Offsets are UTF-16. The cases hold what every port must cut identically.

hunks.out: [{old_start, old_end, new_start, new_end}] in UTF-16 units

cases.why: the common prefix comes first: of two equal neighbours the EARLIER is kept, so the second one is deleted
same rule on a repeated word: the prefix takes the first copy
text typed after a copy is an insertion after it
prefix, then suffix, and the middle is what was typed
the common suffix « es » is kept, the rest is one replacement
the middle is compared by longest common subsequence: c and d stay, two replacements
a character outside the basic plane is ONE unit of the diff, and its offsets count both UTF-16 units
the unit is the code point, not the grapheme: the combining mark is deleted, the base letter stays (the editor snaps selections to graphemes)
the prefix is taken first, then the suffix of what is left of BOTH: the overlap is never counted twice
